newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi's Buyoya confirms talks with Hutu rebels.
newsitem.headline: Burundi's Buyoya confirms talks with Hutu rebels.

text.p: Burundi's military ruler Pierre Buyoya said on Tuesday his government made progress towards a ceasefire during direct talks with the main Hutu rebel group the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD).
"We had a meeting with CNDD in Rome in order to obtain a ceasefire and to stop the fighting," Buyoya told a news conference.
"With CNDD we agreed all the steps necessary to get a ceasefire," Buyoya said.
He gave no details of the date of the talks or who represented each side.
The CNDD's armed wing the Forces for the Defence of Democracy is the main Hutu group engaged in a bitter civil war against Burundi's army.
It is the first time Buyoya, who took power in an army coup last July, has confirmed talks with the rebels. Up to now senior officials have denied the talks, fearing a backlash from extremist Tutsis.

Buyoya said a sovereign "National Conference", to include all parties including rebels based outside the country, would be held as part of a three-stage dialogue. He gave no timetable for the process.
"For us it was a meeting to create the conditions in order to open the dialogue between all Burundians for peace and reconciliation," he said.
Regional states made unconditional talks between the government and rebels a condition of lifting sanctions imposed last July after the coup, but the blockade was eased last month.
More than 150,000 people have died in Burundi since October 1993 when the country's first freely-elected president was murdered by Tutsi troops in an attempted coup.
